sources.entry: MistServer - Public domain streaming media server that works with any device and any format. (Source Code) Unlicense C++

summary.one_liner: MistServer is an open source streaming media toolkit for OTT (internet) streaming, built to run on many devices and formats.
summary.what_it_does: MistServer is a modular streaming media server written in C++ and distributed under the public domain (Unlicense). A MistController binary starts the system, scans its directory for other Mist* binaries, and runs them to discover available inputs, outputs and processes, so unwanted binaries can simply be deleted. The controller listens on port 4242 for API connections and serves a web interface for most API commands. Running it in a terminal walks through a first-time setup, or that setup can be completed in the web interface. The README describes it as a full-featured, next-generation toolkit aimed at developers and system integrators. Pre-compiled binaries are offered for common operating systems, with an install command that sets it up under the system init daemon (systemd recommended). Full manual and API specifications are referenced externally.
use_cases: stream live video over the internet
serve media to any device or format
build a custom streaming platform via API
run a streaming media server under systemd
notable: Modular design: MistController auto-discovers Mist* binaries, so unneeded components can be removed
Web interface and API on port 4242 for configuration
Meson wraps resolve dependencies automatically, preferring system libraries when compatible
caveats: CMake build support was discontinued in version 3.4; Meson is the only supported build system
Contribution guidelines are stated as forthcoming; contributors are directed to email
Full documentation and API specs are hosted externally, not in the README
